batchName: Empire: From Constantine's Sons to Theodosius (AD 337-395) - Latin words
chapterName: Empire: From Constantine's Sons to Theodosius (AD 337-395)
description: Written by hand from the chapter text: the Latin words it explains

questions.question: Valens let the Goths cross the Danube as foederati. What were they?
questions.explanation: He hoped for farmers and soldiers; cheating officials pushed them into revolt.
questions.sourceQuote: let them cross the Danube as allies (*foederati*)

questions.question: What does Vicisti, Galilaee mean?
questions.explanation: The legend of Julian’s last words is considered invented.

questions.question: Julian was proclaimed Augustus at Lutetia. Which city is that?
questions.explanation: His soldiers mutinied rather than march east.
questions.sourceQuote: proclaimed Julian Augustus, senior emperor, at Paris (*Lutetia*).

questions.question: Julian wanted to be primus inter pares. What does it mean?
questions.explanation: He joined Senate debates as an ordinary member.
questions.sourceQuote: Julian wanted to be first among equals (*primus inter pares*)

questions.question: Arbogast was magister militum in the west. What was that?
options: Master of soldiers, the top general
questions.explanation: He put a puppet emperor on the throne in 392.
questions.sourceQuote: the western master of soldiers (*magister militum*)

questions.question: Julian handed power back to the curiae. What were they?
questions.explanation: He also cancelled unpaid land taxes.

questions.question: Julian won his great battle at Argentoratum in 357. What is it today?
questions.explanation: Heavily outnumbered, the Romans drove the Alamanni into the Rhine.

questions.question: Julian’s rival in Gaul was the praefectus praetorio. What was his job by then?
questions.explanation: Julian blocked his tax increase and clashed with him over corruption.
questions.sourceQuote: Gaul's top civil official, the praetorian prefect (*praefectus praetorio*)
